name: sm11
about: Kuman SM11 smart car kit, 4WD (the user, 2026-11-21): Uno R3, L298N-style EN+IN board, 4 TT 1:48 gearmotors (2 in parallel per channel), 2x18650, carrying the Pi 5 and the iPhone. Geometry (track, wheelbase, body) is estimated from the user's photo with the 65 mm TT wheel as scale; NOTHING here is measured yet: every value is a guess from the firmware constants, datasheets and TT-motor folklore. Replace them when the car arrives (see measure_when_the_car_arrives). sm11_2wd.json is the 2WD variant.
measure_when_the_car_arrives: 1. Battery: multimeter across the battery box, idle (batt_v) and while 'D 1 1' runs on the floor (sag -> batt_r_ohm ~= (V_idle - V_load) / ~1.2 A for 4WD). Then the worst case: watch the meter (min/max mode) during 'R 90' from rest; compare with the bench truth's batt_v_low for the same TURN.

2. Straight speed: python3 iter1-wasd/laptop/wheel_cal.py dc-move (docs/PI_TEST.md Step 5) on the demo floor. The saved mm_s is the car's speed at D 1 (duty 0.45). In the bench: adjust kv_mps_per_v until 'M 1000' with the firmware's default 150 mm/s lands where the real car did (or run bench/tests/test_car.py's calibration step and compare its recovered mm_s with yours).

3. Spin: wheel_cal.py dc-spin (deg_s at D 1) -> track_eff_m = 2 * v_D1 / radians(deg_s). If the car does NOT turn at all (buzzes in place: the 4WD tyre-scrub stall this profile predicts at the firmware's 0.45 duty cap), that is the finding: note it, then find the lowest spin duty that turns ('D 1 -1' is capped, so: reflash with a higher DC_MAX_DUTY, or test with wheels on a smooth board) and set scrub_mu so the bench stalls/turns at the same duty. dc-spin --slow (duty 0.36) the same way.

4. Drift: 'M 1000' on the floor, measure the sideways miss d (m) -> heading change ~= 2*d/1 rad; set gain_l/gain_r so the bench curves the same way (or trim DC_LEFT_GAIN/DC_RIGHT_GAIN in tars.ino, then put gains back to 1).

5. Deadband: wheels in the air, 'D x x' from rest with the kick disabled is not possible without reflashing; instead creep 'D 0.05 0.05' up until a ROLLING wheel keeps going (v_keep = duty * (batt_v - driver_drop_v)).
6. Geometry: tape-measure track_m (left-right wheel centres), wheelbase_m (front-rear axles), length_m / width_m (outermost points, incl. wheels and anything mounted). Weigh the loaded car (mass_kg).
7. Driver: read the chip on the board. L298N: keep ch_limit_a 2.0 / driver_r_ohm 1.2. L293D-style: ch_limit_a 0.6, driver_drop_v ~1.4, driver_r_ohm ~2. Count the motors per side (motors_per_side).

8. Brownout: with the Pi's USB unplugged (Uno on the kit battery only), run 'R 90' and 'D 1 1' from rest 10x on a half-flat battery; any READY in the serial monitor = a reset. No reset -> lower uno_resets_below_v until the bench agrees; with USB from the Pi plugged in, set it to 0.
9. Flip 'measured' to true and write the date + how in 'source' for every value you replace.

batt_v.source: 2x18650 nominal (PI_TEST §2b: 2x18650 typical, 8.4 V fresh / ~7.0 V flat; kit battery unverified)

batt_r_ohm.source: guess: two cheap 18650 cells + holder springs + switch

driver_drop_v.source: L298N datasheet VCEsat(H)+VCEsat(L): ~2.5 V typ at 1 A, ~3.7 V at 2 A -> 1.3 V + 1.2 ohm x I (with driver_r_ohm). Gives the old 1.8 V at a 2WD's ~0.4 A, ~2.2-2.5 V at a 4WD's 0.8-1 A. Driver chip itself unverified (PI_TEST 2b)

kv_mps_per_v.source: chosen so duty 0.45 (DC_MAX_DUTY) at 7.4 V gives 150 mm/s, the firmware's DC_MM_S_DEFAULT; also ~0.66 m/s at 6 V = the TT 1:48 '200 rpm' rating on a 65 mm wheel. Wheel: 65 mm TT (photo), which this speed already assumes

v_keep.source: just under DC_MIN_DUTY 0.30 x (7.4-1.8) = 1.68 V, so the firmware's minimum duty keeps a rolling wheel going (tars.ino DC tuning comment)

v_start.source: guess: above DC_MIN_DUTY so the 0.80 x 40 ms kick (DC_KICK_*) is what starts a wheel, as the firmware assumes

scrub_v.source: guess: extra spin loss besides tyre scrub (gearbox back-driving, wiring); tyre scrub is now scrub_mu x geometry

motor_r_ohm.source: TT motor folklore: ~0.8-1 A stall at 6 V

tau_s.source: guess: 0.08 s was for 1 motor/side + 0.5 kg; this car is ~0.85 kg; with motors_per_side 2 the model uses tau_s/2 = 0.07 s

brake_tau_s.source: guess: BRAKE_ON_STOP shorts the motor (PI_TEST §2b 'stops dead')

gain_l.source: matched sides; the real pair differs (490 vs 980 Hz EN PWM, tars.ino DC_*_GAIN comment)

slip.source: guess: rubber TT wheels on a hard floor

drift_deg_per_m.source: 0 here; iter2-autonomy/goto/tests/test_dc_car.py sweeps +-15 deg/m as the bad case

track_eff_m.source: 0 = derive: track_m x (1 + (wheelbase_m/track_m)^2) = 0.207 m with the photo geometry (was 0.264 with the old guesses; goto's test_dc_car.py uses 0.20). Calibration (step 3) writes the measured value here

bump_g_per_mps.source: chosen so a 150 mm/s wall hit (2.4 g) passes the firmware's 1200 mg BUMP_THRESHOLD_MG

uno_resets_below_v.source: worst case: the Uno runs only off the kit battery (VIN regulator dropout ~1.1 V under 5 V + margin). BUT with the Pi's USB cable plugged in, the Uno R3 switches its 5 V rail to USB when VIN < ~6.6 V, so it would not reset: set 0 for that case (PI_TEST 2b power notes)

boot_ms.source: Uno R3 Optiboot after a DTR reset (~1.5 s, motor_uno_serial.c comment) + setup()

imu.source: MPU6050 fitted on A4/A5 (the kit has none: without one tip/bump is off; set 0 to test that)

motors_per_side.source: the user: the car is 4WD; each side's two TT motors share one driver channel (PI_TEST 2b)

driver_r_ohm.source: L298N datasheet saturation voltage vs current (see driver_drop_v)

ch_limit_a.source: L298N: 2 A per channel DC. If the board turns out to be L293D-style, set 0.6 (4WD stall ~1.2 A per channel would hit it)

track_m.source: estimated from photo, 65 mm TT wheel as scale (the user's photo of the real car, 2026-11-21): tyre centre to tyre centre ~13 cm (was a 0.155 guess)

wheelbase_m.source: estimated from photo, 65 mm TT wheel as scale (the user's photo of the real car, 2026-11-21): axle to axle ~10 cm (was a 0.13 guess)

mass_kg.source: guess: kit + 2x18650 ~0.45 kg, Pi 5 + its 5 V supply ~0.2 kg, iPhone ~0.2 kg. No better basis from the photo: kept

scrub_mu.source: guess, kept at 0.4: the photo shows wide, soft-looking rubber TT tyres, which argues for MORE sideways grip (0.5-0.8 on a grippy floor), not less; 0.4 is the hard-floor/smooth-tile middle. ~0.3 smooth tile with hard tyres, ~0.8 soft rubber on grippy floor; carpet differs

motor_n_per_v.source: TT 1:48 folklore: ~0.8 kgf.cm stall at 6 V on a 32.5 mm wheel = 2.4 N, over (6 - v_keep) V

length_m.source: the user, 2026-11-21: car is ~0.40 m long and 0.30 m wide incl. side buffers (not tape-measured); was a photo guess

width_m.source: the user, 2026-11-21: car is ~0.40 m long and 0.30 m wide incl. side buffers (not tape-measured); was a photo guess

brown_hold_ms.source: guess: the Uno/driver board's capacitors ride through shorter dips
